content.text: , are you handling the Eventing spec? If so, I think we will want to factor this into that, no?
Yes, we should certainly factor this into the spec.
See:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1008
for the original conversation.
Here is a draft of an event ontology.
And by "draft", I mean the sort you find in old 1800's Vermont farmhouses, which are usually indications that you need a professional to take a good look at it before you really feel comfortable.
https://github.com/acoburn/fcrepo-event-ontology
Looks good, thanks for moving this forward. I do have some questions:
1. Why break up the URI into "root" and "resource path"?
2. Do we not have something we can import for timestamp? Maybe from PREMIS or somewhere?
3. Ditto for "user"?
The reason to break up root and resource path has everything to do with how transactions work in Fedora – to start a transaction, one needs to know the location of the Root.

So in a messaging context, if I want to start a transaction, I need to issue that request to the root location. If the message simply has the root and the path concatenated, then the client would need special
a priori
knowledge about where that root location is.
Another thought was the multi-tenancy context. While this isn't relevant at present, if there were multiple roots, I can imagine that it would be
extremely
convenient for a messaging system to be able to route based on the value of the root URI.
I am not wedded to that division, but it would make certain operations significantly easier for a client.
The premis vocabulary contains
premis:hasEventDateTime
which seems like an excellent match for the timestamp property. Premis also includes
premis:hasEventRelatedAgent
, though it seems from the documentation that a subProperty such as
http://id.loc.gov/vocabulary/preservation/eventRelatedAgentRole/aut
is preferred.
Either way, seems like we can remove the timestamp and user-related fields from this ontology.

Your arguments about "root" make sense. I'm not happy about the fact that you have to go to the root to start a transaction, but that's not a problem in this ticket. And the multi-tenancy thing is a very strong argument. But in this case, we're not really talking about "root", are we? We're talking about some kind of "outermost container"? Or maybe I'm worrying too much about the language.
The language could be "topMostThing", for all I care. The current language uses
org.fcrepo.jms.baseUrl
; I changed it to "root" in this ontology because it refers to the
fedora:RepositoryRoot
resource, which seemed a better description of this thing (e.g. so as not to confuse it with a servlet's "context path", which might be /fcrepo rather than /fcrepo/rest).
"root" is better than "baseUrl", to my eye. I think we have two things here, as was hinted at by

in a different context. There is the repository root, which is a syntactic thing, and there is the "top" or "outermost" container, which is a semantic thing. It's the second one we care about here, right?
Yes, here I believe we are interested in the top/outermost container, as defined by the repository. Syntactically, that means the resource that has the
fedora:RepositoryRoot
type, but that's just the logical outcome of the semantics of that URL representing the outermost container.

I think you mean the URL is the syntactical element and the typing is the semantic construct, right? That identity of syntactical construct and semantic construct only occurs right now because we haven't got clear on PUT yet. I don't think we want to assume it going forward.
Ah, yes, that is what I meant.
I have updated
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-event-ontology
to use the PROV ontology to express events from the messaging system. An example in compact JSON-LD is provided, using the provided context.json in that git repo.

This further shrinks the potential event ontology to contain only three classes (event:ResourceCreation, event:ResourceDeletion, event:ResourceModification). All properties come from other, existing ontologies (prov, dc, dcterms and foaf).
I looked into using premis for this, but ultimately, PROV proved to be a much more natural fit.

Much of this looks very good to me. I don't understand, though, why we are putting requirements (i.e. "Each event will contain the following required data:") into an ontology, which cannot enforce them?
No, we certainly can't enforce that in the ontology, nor is the ontology structured to do that.

Perhaps the confusion has to do with the fact that the README conflates a description of the ontology and an application profile specific to Fedora's messaging system (which is clearly out of scope from the perspective of the ontology).

And as I am thinking about this more, the ontology here is now down to defining just three classes: Create, Update and Delete. It seems like there must be a vocabulary out there with the basic CRUD operations. If such a thing exists (I couldn't find one – there's the HTTP ontology, but that's not quite right), it would mean this ontology is completely unnecessary, and we're down to just an application profile defined in the context of the spec.
I have updated the event ontology README to more clearly distinguish between the ontology and the application profile for Fedora events.
+1 to this.
One question is
this line
a mistake or does some black magic cause it to change in another context?
That was a mistake. Thanks for catching that. I updated that line to point to the Duraspace wiki page for the Messaging SPI – not that that page is particularly helpful at this point.
This looks good:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-event-ontology
I would be inclined to move this forward by publishing the "event" ontology and letting refinement happen with time.
For consistency, would you be opposed to going with the date-based versioning:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-labs/fcrepo-event-ontology/blob/master/event.ttl#L13
..instead of "v0" ?
I have reformatted this ontology as RDF/XML and included an XSLT for HTML display. Furthermore, it uses a version label that is consistent with other ontology versioning schemes.
A related question is: at what point should this repository move out of -labs (and should the ontology be added to an existing git repo or should it stay separate)?
I think it ready to move out now, but as to where… that is not as clear to me.
See fcrepo PR here:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1053
Given the core-nature of the fcrepo-event-ontology, it seems fitting for it to move into:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/ontology
This looks good, pending response to internal and external audit comments.
Related PR for fcrepo-audit:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-audit/pull/35
..and:
https://github.com/acoburn/fcrepo4/pull/5
, If you merge:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-audit/pull/35
into master
I will merge:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/pull/1053
And close this ticket.
fcrepo-audit PR merged via:
https://github.com/fcrepo4-exts/fcrepo-audit/commit/d85bb9a4b684d2a93448655bc93490afa008a2ba
is welcome to merge the related fcrepo4 PR at his leisure.
Along with the above, this is the primary resolution:
https://github.com/fcrepo4/fcrepo4/commit/ddee309f31c63daac5a42de4da6bdabfc2d45c92

Fedora should publish as part of the ontologies a system of classes and predicates (mostly reusing extant work) for the encoding of published events, such as appear on the Java API's event bus and are currently translated into JMS. Of course, the JMS event tap should also
use
this encoding.
